messages:
sam: heads-up - after landing the kernel switch last night we're seeing a rise in soft 429s on p50/p90 for gen routes. noticed batch sizes dropped ~20% and kv-hit rate dipped from 84% -> 67%

maria: ugh. which kernel exactly? the one that changed fused-attn path?

sam: yeah, landed patch `opt/fused-prefetch-v2` (commit 7c9f3). perf CI looked fine but prod traces show longer per-batch assembly time and more single-request microbatches.

lee: any evidence it's batching heuristic mismatch vs kernel latency change? could be kernel increased variance so our batch formation timer fires earlier.

sam: that's my hypothesis. profiler screenshots: `latency_histogram(batch_assembly_ms)` shifted - median same, tail higher; drivers show slower kernel dispatch for seq_len < 64.

jonah: what about token-budget targets? if we lowered token_budget_target recently that could make admit tighter.
maria: token_budget_target is still at 128k in production for gen-high. no recent changes there.

ops-bot: deploy finished: opt/fused-prefetch-v2 by @sam at 2026-03-17T23:10:12Z :rocket:

lee: can you paste a sample of the admission log lines around a 429? want to see reason codes (KV_MISS vs BATCH_TIMEOUT vs TOKEN_BUDGET)
sam: pasted below:
```
[1769456801] admit_decision: queue_len=12, batch_assembling_ms=47, token_budget_remain=34000, kv_hit_ratio=0.67, decision=soft_reject(prob=0.6), reason=BATCH_TIMEOUT
[1769456810] admit_decision: queue_len=8, batch_assembling_ms=15, token_budget_remain=41200, kv_hit_ratio=0.71, decision=accept, kernel_variant=fused-prefetch-v2
[1769456823] admit_decision: queue_len=15, batch_assembling_ms=62, token_budget_remain=10200, kv_hit_ratio=0.65, decision=hard_reject, reason=TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUST
```

jonah: token_budget_remain hitting low is scary. are we leaking budget due to duplicated estimates on KV misses?
maria: good call - kvcache miss causes extra prefix tokens in accounting. we recently added separate accounting for prefetch overhead but maybe it's double-counting.

lee: for quick mitigation I propose: 1) temporary relax token_budget_target by +25% for gen-high pools, 2) widen batch_assembly_timeout by +10ms when kernel variant reports seq_len<64, 3) add a probabilistic soft-shed fallback to accept 10% of soft_rejects to avoid cascading hard rejects.
sam: agree. can we A/B the relax by region? europe has most of the incidents.

jonah: I'll push a canary: set token_budget_target=160k for pool gen-high-eu for 1h, and adjust batch_timeout from 20ms -> 30ms only on fused-prefetch-v2. also enable soft-accept with seed=0xdead.
maria: also rolling back the prefetch accounting change would remove the double count if it's bugged — but that's riskier. maybe we instrument accounting counters first.

ops-bot: rollout plan created: canary -> 10% -> full. triggered by @jonah

sam: test run looks promising. after increasing budget canary p95 429s dropped 60% and average batch size recovered from 3.2 -> 3.9

lee: long-term we need kernel-aware admission: feed kernel latency distribution into batch target heuristics so assembly timeout and token budgets adapt per kernel_variant + seq_len histogram. also add a kvcache-miss correction factor in token accounting to not double-charge prefetch overhead.

maria: filed RFC: "kernel-aware-admission-and-kv-accounting" with perf traces and suggested equations for dynamic token budgeting. attaching snippet of heuristic formula we tested:
```
batch_timeout_ms = base_timeout + alpha * p95_kernel_dispatch_ms[variant,seq_bucket]
token_budget_target = base_token_budget * (1 + beta * (1 - kv_hit_ratio))
```
where alpha=0.3, beta=0.6 looked reasonable in sim.

jonah: action items: 1) canary relax token budget (in flight) 2) instrument kv-accounting counters (maria) 3) sim kernel-aware heuristics on replay data (lee) 4) revert kernel if soft-accept mitigation fails (sam)
sam: I'll also add a perf trace tag in logs `kernel_variant` and `seq_bucket` so we can slice quickly.

lee: thanks. keep updates here. if we still see heavy hard_reject/TOKEN_BUDGET_EXHAUST after canary we revert. :thumbsup:

maria: noted. I'll post KV counters in 30m.

jonah: canary metrics after 15m: p50 latency stable, p90 gen route latency -3% -> +2% (within noise), p95 429 rate -58% vs baseline. kv_hit_ratio on canary unchanged (68%). canary looks safe to increment to 25%.

sam: perfect. pushing to 25% now.

ops-bot: rollout to 25% completed by @jonah at 2026-03-18T00:10:42Z

lee: great work thread. we'll follow up in RFC PR and schedule a short postmortem if we end up reverting.

maria: posting logs and counters in #eng-runtime-ops later today.

sam: closing loop when full rollout done. anyone want to add anything?

jonah: nbd, thanks all. :raised_hands:"
